summary: The article describes how AI has transformed climate science since September 2023, from high-resolution forecasting and real-time monitoring to disinformation detection, tailored regional solutions and AI-generated hypotheses. It walks through a timeline of projects and tools, each tied to a named researcher or organization. It concludes that AI is a transformative force for understanding, predicting and mitigating climate change.
one_line: A timeline of AI advances in climate science since September 2023, covering forecasting models, disinformation tools, real-time monitoring and AI-generated climate theories.
key_facts: Dr. Rachel Tan of the Climate Analytics Institute led a team that integrated a state-of-the-art AI system into climate modeling on October 15, 2023.
Since November 22, 2023, major environmental agencies have used AI to fine-tune climate models, producing high-resolution forecasts at community level.
The International Climate Alliance unveiled the HYPERION model on December 5, 2023; it uses machine learning to simulate weather patterns in far greater detail than previous models.
Dr. Kenneth Liu, a meteorologist, said HYPERION can give specific regions advanced warnings about shifts in weather patterns, 'potentially saving lives'.

Professor Angela Hart of the University of Global Change introduced the AI platform ClimaTruth on February 8, 2024, which uses natural language processing and sentiment analysis to identify and rectify misleading climate information online.
Dr. Sandra Higgs and her EarthData.AI team merged AI with satellite imaging and IoT-sourced datasets on March 26, 2024, creating TerraVision AI for real-time analysis of environmental changes.
Dr. Higgs said TerraVision AI lets researchers see the impact of conservation efforts and policy changes 'within weeks instead of years'.
Dr. Omar Patel's global consortium EcoSynthAI has been operational since April 12, 2024, tailoring climate interventions to regional ecological and socio-economic conditions.
On May 25, 2024, an AI system called Athena, originally designed to improve models, began proposing new theories about climatic interactions and human impact.
Dr. Eric Duval, one of Athena's lead architects, said Athena is 'theorizing, creating hypothesis' that open new avenues in climate science.
Tel Aviv-based startup GreenMind AI emerged at the Climate Innovation Forum on July 5, 2024, using neural networks to predict which conservation efforts work best in different ecosystems.
GreenMind AI founder Dr. Yael Stein said AI is used 'not just to predict the future but to proactively shape it towards sustainability'.
